title: Baumgart's conjecture that every graphic matroid is SIBO
statement:
A rank-$r$ matroid is **subsequence-interchangeably base orderable (SIBO)** if every pair of bases $A$ and $B$ admits orderings $a_1,\ldots,a_r$ of $A$ and $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B$ such that

$$
(B\setminus\{b_i,\ldots,b_j\})\cup\{a_i,\ldots,a_j\}
$$

is a basis for every $1\le i\le j\le r$. **Baumgart's conjecture.** Every graphic matroid is SIBO. If true, this would imply the proximity conjecture for graphic matroids; the conjecture is presented as open in the paper.
source_name: Dániel Garamvölgyi, Ryuhei Mizutani, Taihei Oki, Tamás Schwarcz and Yutaro Yamaguchi, “Towards the Proximity Conjecture on Group-Labeled Matroids”, arXiv:2411.06771 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.06771

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of November 2024). “Sparse paving matroids are significant in matroid theory as they have been used in hardness proofs for several algorithmic problems as well as counterexamples of conjectures.”
